notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); gate.digest is the digest line of the last gate run. Model-authored and unreviewed: no hardware run and no human review is claimed. The upstream Ant environment needs the external NVIDIA Isaac Gym Preview 4 simulator and a CUDA device (README.md:13-14), so the sim backend was not run and the clone was never imported or executed. The fake is a pure Python kinematic stand-in, not the card's upstream-sim mock strategy, which the hard rules forbid; it serves the upstream 60-element observation layout and the 8-value action Box but has no rigid-body dynamics or contacts, so the deployed model is F0 with the gaps listed in driver.py. The upstream uses legacy Gym 0.23.1 (setup.py:17); the bridge accepts its four-tuple step, and the fake returns the Gymnasium five-tuple. NOT COVERED: the real Isaac Gym state, including contact forces and actuator torques; the fake returns the 24-element contact block as zeros. The five warnings are expected of a Gymnasium family driver and match the exemplar: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge stores the pending seed and applies it on the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived world inputs. No Limits are declared: the action Box (-1..1 per element) and the ticks bound are derived by the bridge. No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. task.json was not edited; the clone is untouched.
